response.rationale: Both answers and the English cue are materially correct. “Bunga” is the ordinary Indonesian banking term; Malaysian Malay ordinarily uses “faedah,” although Malaysian dictionaries also recognize “bunga” as a financial synonym. Thus “different-common-word” is acceptable as a default-usage contrast, but not an absolute lexical distinction. No false-friend contrast is present or required.
